Q3 Latency Investigation

Draft prepared by an agent · generating…

This report summarises the p99 latency regression observed across the API fleet during the third quarter. The numbers below are drawn from the request-tracing pipeline and have not yet been reconciled against the billing export.

Every figure in this section should be treated as provisional until the reconciliation job has run against the full quarter.

Regression summary

Three services account for nearly all of the increase. The remaining services stayed within their historical envelope and are excluded from the table for brevity.

Service p50 (ms) p99 (ms) Change
checkout-api 42 1,180 +340%
search-index 18 640 +120%
media-transcode 310 4,900 +88%
auth-edge 9 72 +4%

The reconciliation job has not yet been run against the full quarter.

Probable causes

  • Connection-pool exhaustion during the 14:00 UTC batch window.
  • A cache key change shipped in week 6 that halved the hit rate.
  • Cross-region failover that was never reverted after the June test.

The second item is the most likely primary cause. The cache key change was shipped without a migration, so every warm key was orphaned at deploy time rather than expiring gradually. 

// The offending change — note the missing version prefix.
- cacheKey = `v2:${tenant}:${query}`
+ cacheKey = `${tenant}:${query}`

Recommended next steps

Restore the version prefix and backfill the orphaned keys before the next batch window. The connection-pool ceiling should be raised only after the cache hit rate has recovered, otherwise the two changes cannot be told apart in the traces.

The reconciliation job has not yet been run against the full quarter.

Once both changes are in place, a follow-up pass over the same tracing window will confirm whether the regression is fully resolved or whether the failover path is contributing an independent share.
